title: Incremental deploy safety profiles and enforcement engine
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a reusable set of 'safety profiles' and an enforcement layer that compiles those profiles into traffic-split schedules, guardrail checks, and automated rollback actions for incremental model deployments (canaries, A/B experiments, and shadow testing). Goal is to provide teams with pre-baked templates (Conservative / Balanced / Fast) and an engine that executes them reliably across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
background: We currently have ad-hoc rollout scripts and several infra-level testbed implementations that are inconsistent across teams. SREs and platform engineers repeatedly tune traffic split heuristics and guardrails. Product teams need a simple, audit-friendly way to run incremental experiments without recreating the same safety checks. This ticket consolidates policy design and builds an enforcement engine that integrates with rollout orchestration and our existing metrics/alerting stacks.
goals: Create three opinionated safety profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) that map to parameterized traffic schedules and guardrail thresholds
Implement a policy compiler that converts a profile into an executable rollout plan (time/step/split) and runtime guard checks
Integrate guardrail evaluation with metric sources: latency p50/p95, request error rate, hallucination score (eval set), user-visible degradation metrics
Support shadow traffic and A/B mode metadata tagging so experiments are tracked in analytics and billed appropriately
Provide automatic rollback and manual-approval hooks with clear audit logs and reasons
non_goals: Full control-plane UI for editing profiles (we will provide a CLI and config schema; Console integration is follow-up)
Replacing existing experiment statistical engine for A/B inference (we will export labeled results to the analytics pipeline instead)
enforcement_rules:
- Compile profile into a finite-state rollout controller.
- At each step, evaluate guardrails during a watch window equal to step.duration_minutes / 2.
- If a guardrail is violated twice within the watch window, trigger immediate rollback to previous stable variant and create an incident.
- If a non-critical signal (minor latency blip) occurs, throttle further traffic increases but do not rollback; re-evaluate after a cooldown period.
- Shadow traffic runs are logged and never counted towards production split but feed eval pipelines.
- A/B tests annotate traffic with cohort tags and emit per-cohort metrics to analytics with cohort-specific thresholds.
rollout_steps_example: Conservative profile example: [ step 1: 5% for 60m (watch 30m), step 2: 10% for 120m (watch 60m), step 3: 25% for 240m (watch 120m), step 4: 50% for 24h ]
metrics_to_track: tail CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth
hallucination / semantic-regression score from canonical eval set
user-visible failure signals (chat abandons, rapid retries)
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema is documented and committed as a spec in Confluence
Compiler converts profiles into rollout plans that can be executed by the rollout controller (integration test coverage >= 80%)
Guardrail checks wire up to production metrics and publish violation events to the incident pipeline
Auto-rollback executes within SLA for rollback (< 2 minutes from trigger) and creates a provenance record with reason
Shadow traffic path delivers request copies to target variant without affecting billing for production paths and is visible in analytics dashboards
tasks: Design spec: Confluence doc describing profiles, thresholds, and DSL (owner: Aisha)
Policy compiler: implement translation from profile DSL to rollout plan (owner: Miguel)
Rollout controller: extend existing orchestrator to accept compiled plans and perform step transitions (owner: SRE team)
Guardrail integrations: connect metrics (Prometheus/Kairos) and eval results to guardrail evaluator (owner: Observability)
End-to-end tests: chaos + regression tests that simulate metric violations and validate rollback behavior (owner: Test infra)
Analytics: ensure cohort tagging and shadow logs flow into analytics pipeline (owner: Data infra)
Console hooks: expose profile selection and rollout logs (follow-up UI ticket)
risks: False positives in hallucination/regression detector could cause unnecessary rollbacks
Metric delays or aggregation windows could mask fast failures leading to insufficient protection
Complexity of supporting distinct behaviors across Hosted/Dedicated/Private could increase maintenance burden
Performance overhead of guardrail checks under very high QPS if naive polling is used
decisions: Use profile templates rather than free-form DSL for v1 to reduce user error
Default to 'Balanced' profile for onboarding new teams; require explicit opt-in for Aggressive
Implement guardrail evaluation as an event-driven stream consumer (not polling) to reduce latency and load
Auto-rollback will be capped: it can only rollback to the last stable tagged variant and will create a manual review ticket for deeper analysis
